topic.name: The Nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence

question.text: Find the formula for the $n$th term of the arithmetic sequence that has a third term of $6$ and a common difference of $-5.$
question.explanation:
Since $a_{3}=6$ is two jumps after $a_1,$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

\begin{align*} a_{3} &= a_1 + 2d \\[3pt] 6 &= a_1 + 2(-5) \\[3pt] 6 &= a_1 - 10 \\[3pt] 16 &= a_1 \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

\[ \eqalign{ a_n&= a_{1}+(n-1)d\\[3pt] &= 16 + (n-1)(-5) \\[3pt] & = 16 - 5n + 5\\[3pt] &= 21-5n } \]

example.title: Finding the Formula for the Nth Term Given Another Term and the Common Difference

question.text: Find the formula for the $n$th term of the arithmetic sequence that has a $17$th term of $99$ and a common difference of $4.$
question.explanation:
Since $a_{17}=99$ is $16$ jumps after $a_1,$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

\begin{align*} a_{17} &= a_1 + 16d \\[3pt] 99 &= a_1 + 16(4) \\[3pt] 99 &= a_1 + 64 \\[3pt] 35 &= a_1 \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is: \[ \eqalign{ a_n&= a_{1}+(n-1)d\\[3pt] & = 35 + (n-1)(4) \\[3pt] & = 35 +4n - 4\\[3pt] &=31+4n } \]

example.title: Finding the Formula for the Nth Term Given Another Term and the Common Difference

question.text: Find the general formula for the $n$th term of the arithmetic sequence that begins with \[ 2, \: 11, \: 20, \: \ldots \]
question.explanation:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

\[ f(n)= f(1)+(n-1)d. \]

From the first few terms

\[ 2, \: 11, \: 20, \: \ldots, \]

we see that the first term is $f(1)=2$ and the common difference is \[ d=11 - 2 = 9. \]

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

\[ \eqalign{ f(n)&= f(1)+(n-1)d\\[3pt] &= 2 + (n - 1)(9) \\[3pt] & =2+9n-9\\[3pt] & =9n-7 } \]

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is $f(n) = 9n-7.$
